paper.title: SteP: Stacked LLM Policies for Web Actions
paper.central_claim: SteP defines an MDP whose state is a stack of LLM policies so that any policy can act, invoke another policy (pushed with an empty history) or terminate and hand control back; dynamic composition of a hand-written library of policies solves a diverse set of web tasks, improving WebArena from 14.9% to 33.5% over SOTA GPT-4 single policies and being competitive on MiniWoB++ with far less data, while using 2.3x fewer tokens than a flat prompt. Scope as measured: WebArena 804 tasks (gpt-4-turbo-preview), MiniWoB++ 45 tasks (text-davinci-003), a self-built airline CRM and three live airline sites (figure only).

Our arithmetic: WebArena n=804 gives SE about 1.6 points per method; SteP 0.33 vs Flat-8k 0.23 is a 10-point gap, about 4 combined SE if sampling noise were the only variance. No repeated-run variance is reported, and per-intent cells in Table 1 are 5 tasks.

Our reading: Flat-4k/Flat-8k are truncated to 4k/8k tokens (E013) while SteP can draw on up to 14 policy prompts of up to 4k tokens each (up to about 56k tokens of authored guidance across the library), so the contrast decomposition-vs-flat is confounded with the amount of authored guidance exposed. The paper does not run an uncapped flat prompt; whether the backbone context allows it is outside the paper (gpt-4-turbo-preview is a long-context model, outside knowledge, unverified here).

Our reading: all 804 WebArena tasks are the test set and the 14 policies were designed by clustering WebArena intents (E009), with coverage of at least 50 of 170 intents; the MiniWoB++ exemplars come from tasks that are also among the 45 evaluated tasks (E026). The only evaluation on sites not used in construction is the live airline experiment, judged against a human demonstration with results in an image.

Searched main text, Tables 1-5, Limitations, Appendices A-D for: a static-hierarchy or non-recursive baseline (DecomP/ADaPT-style) run in the same harness, an ablation that disables recursion or self-invocation, counts of wrong push/pop decisions, wall-clock time, dollar cost, repeated runs or confidence intervals on WebArena, an uncapped flat prompt, per-intent coverage vs gain regression, the maximum step budget, the observation format of the Zhou et al. baseline. None reported; figures are images.

signatures.name: Stacked policy control state
signatures.object: Control flow of a prompted web agent (baseline: one flat policy with a long prompt)
signatures.information: Serialised page text, objective, per-policy local history (observation, reason, action); library of policy descriptions visible to every policy as callable actions.
signatures.operation: Top-of-stack policy emits (a) a web action, (b) an invocation of a library policy (pushed with empty history) or (c) a stop with a return value (popped; value appended to the parent history). The stack can grow recursively.
signatures.conditions: Policies authored by hand; descriptions informative enough for the LLM to choose; return values carry needed state.
signatures.feedback: Environment observations and policy return values.
signatures.selection_rule_data: LLM picks the next call from the policy descriptions; no learned selection.
signatures.persistence: Stack and local histories live within an episode only; the library is a fixed hand-written asset.
signatures.later_use: The library is reused across tasks in the same environment.
signatures.claimed_effect: WebArena 0.23 (Flat-8k) to 0.33; MiniWoB++ few-shot 0.72 (Flat) to 0.96; 22.7K vs 52K tokens.
signatures.failure_boundary: Incomplete information passed to a sub-policy can create an endless loop; communication overhead; manual authoring.

signatures.name: Hand-authored policy library with dedicated instructions and examples
signatures.object: Source of task knowledge in prompts
signatures.information: Author knowledge of the target sites (e.g. which menu to open, filter rules) written as instructions and few-shot examples per policy (up to 4k tokens each).
signatures.operation: Cluster functionally equivalent intents; write a templated prompt per cluster; register it with a description as a callable action for every other policy.
signatures.conditions: Domain knowledge of the sites; policy count small relative to intents covered (at least 50 of 170).
signatures.selection_rule_data: Clustering by the authors on the evaluated intents.
signatures.persistence: Static prompts in the code base.
signatures.claimed_effect: Gains concentrate where policies cover more intents.
signatures.failure_boundary: Coverage gaps leave other intents unimproved; examples elided in the appendix.

signatures.name: Flat control (same guidance in one capped prompt)
signatures.information: All policy instructions and examples concatenated up to 4k or 8k tokens.
signatures.operation: Single policy over a long prompt.
signatures.claimed_effect: Flat 0.20 / 0.23 vs SteP 0.33; some intents regress with longer prompts.
signatures.failure_boundary: The cap means the control does not receive all authored guidance (E044).

retention_trace.reason: The library is hand-written and static; the paper lists automatic discovery of policies from experience as future work. No retained change, selection or later-task improvement loop is claimed.

gap.author_gap: One LLM policy cannot cover the combinatorial open-world tasks and site variation; a big prompt leaks behaviour between unrelated behaviours and long contexts dilute attention; existing decompositions are static hierarchies.
gap.checked_gap: The long-prompt part is supported inside the paper (Flat-4k to Flat-8k gains only 0.20 to 0.23 and some intents regress). The static-hierarchy limitation is argued by example (nested search_list) but no static or non-recursive baseline is run, so its practical size is unverified. Prior WebArena figures (0.12 / 0.15) come from other prompts, models and observation formats.

claims.text: On WebArena SteP reaches 0.33 success, above prior single GPT-4 policies (0.12/0.15) and Flat baselines (0.20/0.23).
claims.setting: All 804 WebArena tasks, gpt-4-turbo-preview, temperature 0.3; 14 hand-written policies of at most 4k tokens each.
claims.baseline_control: Flat-4k and Flat-8k (same instructions and examples, capped), prior numbers from Zhou et al. and Akter et al.
claims.selection_vs_test: Policy library designed by clustering the evaluated intents; all tasks are test.
claims.counterevidence: Flat controls truncated while SteP sees up to 14 policies of guidance (E044); library tuned on test intents (E045); prior numbers use other models and prompts; gains concentrate where policies cover more intents (E011).
claims.allowed_conclusion: With authored, test-intent-informed policies, a stack of LLM policies beats flat prompts capped at 4k/8k tokens by about 10-13 points on WebArena; the decomposition contribution net of authored-guidance volume is not isolated.

claims.text: On MiniWoB++ SteP is competitive with prior work using far less data (0.96 with 10 trajectories).
claims.setting: 45 tasks, 50 seeds per task, text-davinci-003; 7 policies, 21 examples.
claims.baseline_control: Flat zero/few-shot (0.60/0.72), prior methods with different models and data.
claims.selection_vs_test: Exemplars come from tasks that are among the evaluated tasks.
claims.counterevidence: Synapse 0.98 and CC-Net 0.96 are higher or equal; data count excludes authored instructions; Flat gets 7 examples vs SteP 21 (E026).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Competitive with, not better than, the best prior methods, at a lower count of demonstration trajectories but with hand-written policy prompts.

claims.counterevidence: Conditioned on success; extra calls and communication overhead are conceded; wall-clock time not measured.

assessment.author_claim_preserved: dynamic composition of policies improves WebArena from 14.9% to 33.5% and is competitive on MiniWob++ with significantly less data while using 2.3x fewer tokens
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With 14 hand-written, WebArena-intent-informed policy prompts, a policy-stack controller on gpt-4-turbo-preview solves 33% of the 804 WebArena tasks versus 20-23% for flat prompts that are capped at 4k-8k tokens and contain the same material, and uses fewer input tokens per successful trajectory; on MiniWoB++ it is on par with the best in-context methods. Whether the gain comes from decomposition rather than from exposing more authored guidance, and whether dynamic recursion matters, is not isolated; the library is not shown to generalise beyond authored coverage.
unresolved: external code base holds the elided examples
assessment.reproduction: No reproduction run; third-party restatement of the 33.0 figure in AWM and SkillWeaver is author-copied, not a rerun.

G.reason: Specific bottleneck (single long prompt, static hierarchy) with an in-paper diagnostic: longer flat prompts barely help and regress some intents; named neighbours (DecomP, ADaPT, Synapse, state machines). The static-hierarchy residue is argued without a baseline and the authoring cost is conceded.

M.reason: The stack MDP is formal and reconstructable (push/act/pop, local histories, return values) and it directly targets prompt-length and behaviour leakage. The assumption that the LLM can choose the right callee from a description is only exercised, not tested, and the benefit of recursion is not predicted and checked.

X.reason: Algorithm, policy format, most prompts and hyperparameters are given; failure modes (overhead, incomplete information loop, manual library) are stated. In-context examples are elided or external, the step budget is unstated and the wrong-call rate is unmeasured.

E.measurement.reason: WebArena functional-correctness checkers on all 804 tasks and MiniWoB++ built-in rewards are execution-based; AirlineCRM uses an evaluate API against gold actions and live sites are compared to a human demonstration, which is weaker.

E.causality.reason: A same-model Flat control, zero/few-shot sweep, CoT and model-scale ablations exist, but the flat control is capped at 4k/8k tokens while SteP receives the full library, MiniWoB++ Flat has 7 examples vs 21, and there is no non-recursive or static-hierarchy baseline.

E.holdout.reason: All 804 WebArena tasks are test and the library was built by clustering those intents; MiniWoB++ exemplars come from evaluated tasks; the only unseen-site evidence (live airline sites) is figure-only, judged against a human demonstration and undated.

E.statistics.reason: Large denominators (804 tasks, 45x50 seeds, 20 scenarios) and per-site/per-task tables are given, but WebArena is one run at temperature 0.3 with no spread, and several results are only in figures.

E.cost.reason: Input tokens per trajectory, mean actions and the extra communication overhead are reported against the flat baselines, with the limitation conceded; wall-clock time and dollar cost are asserted not measured and the token comparison is conditioned on successful runs.

status_reason: Complete body and appendices read; in-context examples elided in the paper and figure data unavailable are recorded. Pinned AWM and SkillWeaver were read only at passages that cite SteP. All eight items resolved.
readable_summary: System method (policy stack), score 66.3 (66.25), online WebArena/MiniWoB++, claim scoped. Execution-checked results on all 804 WebArena tasks, same-model flat control and cost reporting; but the flat control is truncated to 4k/8k tokens, the 14 policies were authored from the evaluated intents, there is no static or non-recursive baseline, and WebArena is a single run.
